test_title: PYST 39: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 14 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The National Red List Roadmap, launched in October 2025, primarily aims at which of the following?

options.text: To monitor air and water pollution levels across industrial zones
To track progress on renewable energy adoption and emissions reduction
To develop renewable energy targets for environmental sustainability
To assess and monitor the conservation status of the country's flora and fauna

solution:
The correct answer is __**To assess and monitor the conservation status of the country's flora and fauna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Red List Roadmap** was officially launched in **October 2025** as a strategic initiative to systematically evaluate the extinction risk of species within the country.
 
• Its primary objective is to align national conservation efforts with the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** standards to provide a clear picture of the **conservation status** of **flora and fauna**.
 
• The roadmap serves as a guiding document for the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to prioritize species that require immediate protection and habitat restoration.
 
• It facilitates the creation of a comprehensive **National Red List**, which acts as a critical tool for policymakers to allocate funds and resources toward **biodiversity hotspots** and threatened ecosystems. ***Hence, the correct answer is option (4).***
 
• The launch coincided with global efforts to meet the **2030 targets** of the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**, emphasizing the reduction of species extinction rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUCN Red List Categories:**
 
 
• The **IUCN** classifies species into nine groups, including **Extinct (EX)**, **Critically Endangered (CR)**, **Endangered (EN)**, and **Vulnerable (VU)**.
 
• The **National Red List Roadmap** utilizes these global criteria but tailors them to the **regional and national context** of the country's unique biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Involved Organizations:**
 
 
• The **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, established in **1916**, and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**, established in **1890**, are the lead technical agencies responsible for data collection.
 
• These organizations conduct extensive field surveys and **DNA barcoding** to accurately identify and catalog species for the roadmap.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework in India:**
 
 
• The initiative supports the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**, which aims at the conservation of biological resources and equitable sharing of benefits.
 
• It also complements the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, by providing scientific data to update the various **Schedules** that define the legal protection levels for different animals and plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF):** The roadmap is a direct response to **Target 4** of the **Kunming-Montreal GBF**, which mandates urgent management actions to halt human-induced extinction of known threatened species.
 
• **Data Integration:** The roadmap emphasizes the use of **Geographic Information Systems (GIS)** and **Remote Sensing** to track changes in species distribution and habitat loss over time.
 
• **Endemism:** A special focus is placed on **Endemic species** found in regions like the **Western Ghats**, the **Himalayas**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, as these species are found nowhere else in the world and are highly susceptible to climate change.
 
• **Role of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA):** The **NBA**, headquartered in **Chennai**, plays a pivotal role in ensuring that the roadmap's implementation adheres to the **Nagoya Protocol** on access and benefit-sharing.
</ul
